<reason>A high-quality, closely fought debate. PRO built a coherent case (60% enrichment with no civilian purpose, monitoring that recorded rather than prevented, cascades destroyed so the stockpile is inert, a temporary window of Iranian weakness) and answered CON's pressure questions honestly and substantively, especially A1 on intelligence rather than inspectors having found Fordow. But CON made the decisive clash cleaner: the "what you bought vs. what you paid" ledger, the reframe in B4.3 that monitoring's value was forcing any covert effort to be a signature-rich "second program" (which PRO never squarely answered), and the exploitation of PRO's own admissions—A4.7 ("a dash invited exactly this") turned into evidence the unexecuted threat was already working, and A4.3's "buried or in a warehouse" turned into "you cannot threaten an address you cannot name." PRO's closing landed a real counter (a threat never enforced while Iran climbed from 20% to 60% is leverage evaporating), and CON underweighted the destroyed centrifuge-manufacturing base, which keeps PRO's case live. Still, CON's late speeches narrowed the dispute more effectively and gave the reader the more memorable, better-weighed reason to vote. Both sides were clipped for length; PRO twice.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B4.1–B4.3: CON answered PRO's pressure questions directly, converting PRO's A4.7 into proof the unspent threat was coercing Iran at zero cost, and reframing monitoring from "watching" to "making cheating expensive by forcing a whole parallel program"—an argument PRO's "it only kept score" line did not reach.</best_rebuttal>
